# tfcensus rules test

rules test compiles the built-in packs and the rules in a YAML file (a list under rules:, the
same shape as the config key) and reports the first error with the rule name and column.

With --resource, it evaluates every rule against each resource in a JSON file (one object or an
array) and prints the trace: each rule's outcome and the category of the first match. A resource
has the fields a rule sees as resource: account, region, type, source\_type, tf\_types, arn, id,
name, tags, attrs, layer, sources, parents, relationships and created. scan --explain --format
json prints resources in this shape.

Packs, never\_hide and the config's rules come from the loaded config; the file's rules run after
the config's. rules test makes no AWS calls. Expired rules show as expired.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus rules test <rules.yaml> [flags]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Required | Repeatable |
|---|---|---|
| `rules.yaml` | yes | no |

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--resource` | JSON file with a resource or an array of resources to evaluate | string |  |  |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `json`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus rules test rules.yaml
tfcensus rules test rules.yaml --resource sample.json
```
